summary: Asian chip relief continues, but oil remains elevated and US leadership unconfirmed; bearish skew unchanged.
bullish: QQQ recovered 3.73 percentage points from morning observation.
Russell 2000 and Dow closed higher; reported 10Y yield fell.
Equal-weight RSP gained 0.78% while SPY fell 0.30% in a secondary closing report.
FT and WSJ report Asian technology-heavy markets rebounding Thursday; proposed tariffs may replace existing levies rather than stack.
IBD reports Nasdaq-100 futures +1.05% versus S&P futures +0.7% overnight; exact quote time unavailable.
IBD reports both NQ and ES futures up 0.55%; holiday relief persists.
FT reports ASML +2.5% and Stoxx 600 +1.5% Thursday, indicating overseas technology relief.
Reuters reports both Nasdaq and S&P futures approximately +0.7%; Barron's reports +0.7% and +0.8% respectively, exact quote times unavailable.
AP reports Friday Asian gains including Kospi +2.2% and Nikkei +0.7%, supported by chip demand.
bearish: QQQ lagged SPY by 0.36 percentage points at close.
Reuters reports semiconductor and AI credit stress; VIX rose despite recovery.
SMH reportedly lost 8% over five sessions; secondary SOX report indicates severe weakness, exact timestamp unavailable.
Oil supply disruption risk is corroborated by Reuters; inflation sensitivity remains elevated.
Curated core PCE 3.3% versus 3.2% consensus and GDP 4.3% versus 3.6% forecast reinforce tightening risk; tariff proposals are not yet effective.
S&P CreditWatch Negative on Nvidia AA rating adds financing/governance risk; no downgrade or isolated price reaction confirmed.
IBD reports Micron down 4.5% Wednesday; latest reported NQ futures no longer outperform ES.
Reuters reports China reserves the right to respond to tariffs; Korean chipmakers pared early gains according to FT.
Reuters reports Brent $96.25 and WTI $84.78 after renewed reported Middle East supply disruptions; WSJ independently corroborates rising oil. Exact quote times unavailable.

editorial.marketOverview: Friday Asian trading shows renewed risk appetite: AP reports Kospi up 2.2% and Nikkei up 0.7%, with chip demand supportive. AP reports Brent $96.29 and WTI $85.43, without exact quote times. US cash remains closed since Wednesday; QQQ underperformed SPY then.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 20:40 ET snapshot, Asian gains now provide additional evidence of relief, but crude remains elevated. Open Watch refreshed at 02:46 UTC with 181 events and unchanged leading catalysts. No material change in the three-session outlook.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Asian chip buying is constructive but does not establish US SOX leadership. Elevated crude and prior restrictive Fed pricing constrain valuation recovery. The latest available yield pairs are historical, not synchronized with Asian quotes. Oil's prospective US equity impact is not a verified market reaction.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 27: relief potential in a shortened session, with fade risk. Monday November 30: normal liquidity and weekend OPEC+ policy may determine whether relief persists. Tuesday December 1: JOLTS and tentative chip earnings may shift rate expectations and leadership.
editorial.bullCase: Sustained QQQ recovery with SOX outperformance, broad participation, lower volatility and retreating oil would challenge the bearish tilt. Asian technology demand is a supportive but incomplete signal.
editorial.bearCase: Oil staying near recent highs alongside renewed US chip selling and restrictive rate expectations could reverse the relief rally. Tariff and AI financing uncertainty remain unresolved.
editorial.watchNext: Verify NQ versus ES after reopening, SOX relative strength, VXN/VIX, advance-decline breadth and paired Treasury yields. Monitor Friday 13:00 ET close, Sunday OPEC+ and Tuesday JOLTS; confirm issuer earnings dates.
